description: The line plot illustrates how the accuracy of four different models evolves as the number of demonstrations increases on the 'BBQ' task, with the x-axis labeled '#Demonstrations' spanning a linear scale from 0 to 1500 and marked at intervals of 250, and the y-axis labeled 'Accuracy' ranging linearly from 45 to 55 with tick marks every 5 units. The 'Squared Exponential' model, represented by a solid dark blue line with circular markers, begins at approximately 52 accuracy at 0 demonstrations, rises sharply to 56 by 250 demonstrations, and then remains nearly flat through 1500 demonstrations. The 'Tanh' model, shown as a solid medium blue line with circular markers, starts near 48 accuracy at 0 demonstrations and exhibits a slight downward trend, ending at approximately 47 at 1500 demonstrations. The 'ELU' model, depicted with a solid light blue line and circular markers, begins at about 46 accuracy and gradually increases to roughly 48 by 1500 demonstrations. The 'LLaMA-2-chat-7B' model, indicated by a dashed pink line with circular markers, maintains a nearly constant accuracy of 43 across all demonstration counts, showing no discernible trend and remaining substantially below the other three models throughout the range.
caption_used: The line plot illustrates the accuracy of different models as a function of the number of demonstrations, providing a comparison of performance trends on the 'BBQ' task. The x-axis is labeled '#Demonstrations', with a linear scale ranging from 0 to 1500 and tick labels at intervals of 250 demonstrations. The y-axis is labeled 'Accuracy', with a linear scale ranging from 45 to 55, and tick labels at intervals of 5. The 'Squared Exponential' model starts at an accuracy of approximately 52 at 0 demonstrations, increases steadily to 56 at 250 demonstrations, and then stabilizes. The 'Tanh' model begins at about 48 accuracy at 0 demonstrations and shows a slight decline to 47 at 1500 demonstrations. The 'ELU' model starts at 46 accuracy and shows a gradual increase to 48 at 1500 demonstrations. The 'LLmA-2-chat-7B' model maintains a consistent accuracy of 43 across all demonstration points, performing significantly worse than the other models. The 'Squared Exponential' model consistently outperforms all other models, with the 'ELU' model showing the second-best performance overall.
